 This Mfa Filed U/S.173(1) Of Motor Vehicles Act,
Against The Judgment And Award Dated 21.09.2019
Passed In Mvc.No.273/2016 On The File Of The Senior
Civil Judge, Mundaragi, Partly Allowing The Claim
Petition For Compensation And Seeking Enhancement
Of Compensation.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Challenging judgment and award dated 21.09.2019 passed by Senior Civil Judge, Mundaragi, in MVC.no.273/20106, this appeal is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation.
2.
Though above matter is listed for admission, it is taken up for final disposal, with consent of learned counsel for parties.

3. At outset, Sri Siddappa Sajjan, learned counsel for claimants submitted that occurrence of accident involving bus belonging to NWKRTC and death of Hasansab Mulimani in said accident as well as entitlement of claimants for compensation is not in dispute, since respondent - NWKRTC has complied with award.
He submitted that appeal is for enhancement of compensation on limited grounds.

4. It was firstly submitted that as on accident, deceased - Hasansab Mulimani was 28 years of age,
working as fruit seller and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
However, tribunal considered meager monthly income of Rs.6,000/- and awarded inadequate compensation.
It was further submitted that even award under other heads were inadequate and sought enhancement.

Shainaz Begum W/O. Hasansab Mulimani vs The Managing Director on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74306954/
2 5.

sentences.text: On other hand, Sri S.C .Bhuti, learned counsel for - respondents - NWKRTC sought to support award.

6. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and record.
7.

From above submission and since only claimant is seeking enhancement of compensation, point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
8.

Insofar as monthly income, though claimants have stated that deceased was 28 years of age and working as fruit seller and earning Rs.20,000/- per month, no specific evidence is led to substantiate same.
In absence of specific evidence, it has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2016 is Rs.8,750/-.
Therefore, tribunal was error in considering it at Rs.6,000/-.
It has to be considered as Rs.8,750/-.
9. Claimants are wife, four children and mother of deceased - Hasansab Mulimani i.e., six dependents.
Deceased was self-employed.

Therefore, as per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s Pranay Sethi and Ors., reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157,
multiplier applicable would be '17', addition of future prospects would be at '40%' and deduction towards personal expenses would be at '1/4 t h '.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s Pranay Sethi and Ors., reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, total loss of dependency would be as follows:
Rs.8,750/- + 40% -  X 12 X 17 = Rs.18,74,250/-.
10.

Apart from above, claimant no.1 would be entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium, claimants no.2 to 5 would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium, claimant no.6 would be entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of filial consortium.
They would also be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and like sum towards loss of estate.

Since more than 3 years have lapsed after decision in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), 10% has to be added to compensation under conventional heads which would be:
Rs.40,000/- X 6 + Rs.15,000/- X 2 + 10% = Rs.2,97,000/-.
Therefore, total re-assessed compensation would be as follows:
 Sl. Amount in  Conventional Heads  no. Rupees  1. Loss of dependency 18,74,250/-
 2. Loss of consortium  2,40,000/-
 (Rs.40,000/- X 6)
 3. Towards Funeral expenses 15,000/-
 4. Loss of estate 15,000/-
 5. 10% Addition 27,000/-

Total 21,71,250/-

sentences.text: 3 Thus, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

11. Hence, I pass following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
 ii. Claimants are held entitled for  re-assessed compensation of  Rs.21,71,250/- as against Rs.9,88,000/- awarded by tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till its realization.
iii. Respondents - NWKRTC are directed to deposit compensation within eight weeks.

iv. Directions issued by tribunal regarding  apportionment, deposit and release  shall be as per award of tribunal  proportionately to enhanced  compensation.
